title: Stars Don't Really Twinkle
post_description: A star can look like it's blinking, even when its light is steady. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2000-july-25-why-stars-twinkle/ https://starchild.gsfc.nasa.gov/docs/StarChild/questions/question26.html #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Most stars shine with light that is effectively steady to our eyes. The twinkling happens on the way to us. Starlight passes through Earth's turbulent atmosphere, where moving pockets of air bend the light by slightly different amounts. Because stars are so distant, they appear as tiny points, making those changes noticeable as flickering. From above most of Earth's atmosphere, stars do not twinkle in the same way. The atmosphere is doing the visual trick.
